Welcome to Fishing Quinte Forums, a forum about all thing fishing on the Bay of Quinte. This is a new site, there is a discourse app available called ‘Discourse Hub’ in the app store. Download it and add quintefishing.com to access and post on your mobile device.

I have taken over the domain quintefishing.com in an attempt to keep this site going and the exchange of information moving. As a long time quintefishing.com forum member i felt it would be beneficial to keep the exchange of fishing information flowing.

A little about me, I have spent a long time fishing on the Bay of Quinte. While I don’t specifically recall my first cast into the bay, I do recall all the hours I spent fishing off park shorelines around the area at 10 years old. If anyone ever remembers the old government docks and how run down and desolate it was, you would usually see me fishing off the rocks or the end of the pier. This was about as close as i could get as a youngster to all the boats trolling back and forth for Walleye out deeper. But this never deterred me from casting as far as i could to hopefully catch a Walleye. I really wasn’t that successful at catching them, but man did i grind it out. As time went on it eventually paid off ! Eventually graduating to a friends 12’ Sea Nymph aluminum, things got a lot better. It didnt hurt that the majority of my fishing was throughout the 80’s when fishing a little different. We caught tons of fish and made some great memories. It really seems like yesterday to me, analyzing depth charts, getting reports, trying that new lure (seems like the big ones like the wally diver were just coming out then) and taking in the newest fishing technology was a daily ritual.

fast forward a few years, and a few boats later, I was able to lean on countless hours of trial and error. I could talk for hours on it all, but we’re here and now. I still love the Bay, fishing it quite regularly when i can and Lake Ontario fish as well when the weather/wind cooperate. There have been lots of changes to the water and fishing over the years, some good, some what seem bad, but fishing is still great when you can apply your knowledge on patterns and seasonal locations. Some of you who have been here over the years know what I mean. Sometimes it can be a grind, others you are limiting out in an hour. I prefer the latter if I can!

When I had an opportunity to continue Dan Elliot’s quintefishing.com legacy I jumped at the opportunity ! Working in the IT industry for my entire life, I figured I could keep the forum running hopefully as well as Dan was able to. I am hoping you will feel that way as well. I created this site for you, I make nothing from this other than the love of both IT / fishing, and connecting with everyone, kind of a good match

The other hobby of mine, IT/technical stuff, keeps me busy most of the time, but I look forward to any recommendations you may have for this site. It is still in its infancy and may have a few quirks as I go, but my IT side says to keep things always running as smoothly as possible. Please enjoy this site and contribute if you can !

If you need help or have a suggestion, feel free to ask in Site Feedback or contact the admins. Enjoy this site !

Thanks for the efforts! This has been a great forum for a long time. Happy to see it back up!

I’ll be fishing the opener (sun - tues) will post the results.

Cheers CCLad.

My Powerdrive had a few scuffs and I’m pretty anal about keeping my boat shiny so I decided to paint it. A few Youtube video’s but as I have a healthy dose of scepticism about Youtube experts, I didn’t find anything convincing. Also, AI had lots to say but I used it more as a guideline than solid advise.

I spoke to Tim at The Prop Shop and he suggested Tremclad, so sounded like rust paint would work.

I spent some time on the internet and came up with Krylon All-in-one Matte Black. This paint has a built in primer saving a step. I’ve used Krylon before on plastic and it really sticks.

Prep is like anything, the more effort to get it right the better the results. I had one chip I worked on, turned out pretty good but I could have feathered it a bit better. The rest of the motor I gently rubbed down with a 3M Scotch-Brite green pad and a wipe down with paint thinner.

I masked the prop, and motor shaft, have to be real careful with overspray, and a drop cloth for the boat. I left the motor on the boat and extended the shaft using a bungee cord at the head to keep the motor from tipping upright.

I had a day that, according to the instructions, was good for tempurature and very close to humidity. I sprayed 3 very light coats just over a minute in between applications, according to instructions.

Then let it dry. It says 7 days for max hardness and the longer the better. I used my nose and I could smell solvent coming off the paint so maybe a couple more days would be better. I wanted my paint hard so the cradle wouldn’t scuff it up.

I think it turned out very well. The colour and sheen are spot on to the factory finish. The cradle still leaves a rub mark but the bare metal is covered.

If I did it again, I’d spend a bit more time feathering the chip and I’d paint during one the hot weeks in summer. Too hot to fish anyway so might better let paint dry.

I like keeping my boat clean but the Bay water is pretty hard and leaves spots that are tough to get off.
I misted the hull and motor with cleaning vinegar and let is sit for about 10 minutes. Gave it a wash, “no scrubbing” and spots are gone.

A jug of double strength Allen’s vinegar is about $6.00 and will go an awful long way.

I’m guessing the vinegar acid neutralizes the alkaline spots.

Rinsed the boat off really well.

Pleased with the results.

Should have taken a before picture, was pretty bad.

posts.cooked:
Been fishing around Deseronto lately and lots of fish on the finder and a good chunk of boats out there. What’s a lure that’s successful this time of year?

I appreciate this website but I query if it’s in vain(?) I ask this because I’ve never known anglers to give up their spots or tips. Maybe I can be proven wrong but, that seems to be the way..

Thanks all!

Usually you cant go wrong with cranks this time of year. I really only use a handful of lures at any point of time, cranks, spinners, bottom bouncers and jigs. Some faithfuls are CC Shads, Berkley flicker minnows, blue fox #3 spinners, bottom bouncers and any tube or bucktail jigs. Really depends on what they want.

Find a weedline this time of year with green cabbage and you should be on the fish. If the fish move out, dont over look deeper flats. I have had days where i was slamming them off the weed lines, then it went dead, put on cranks and trolled from weed lines all the way out to the main basin and found them there, so many variables. but start with cabbage and cranks are good bet.

If your marking lots of fish, large marks, they are probably sheep head. Theres millions of them this time of the year in the bay, so dont stick around if they are only sheep. Walleye are hard to mark on the sounders as they stick on the bottom pretty close. They usually look like smaller fish or ‘anomalies’ on your finder right on the bottom. Run your cranks over their head, if they are hungry, they will come up for it. As for the cabbage, you just wont mark them there at all, but i use my finder to find weed edges if they are deeper.

Hope this helps.
Thank You so kindly for your in-depth answer . That’s very helpful! Are you tipping the crankbaits with live bait?

no nothing on cranks, cant go wrong with a rapala shad rap or CC Shad if you can find them though.

I only tip spinners and bottom bouncers, make sure you work over weed lines first, you will usually find them there this time of year.

Fishing’s been good late May into June. Lots of small ones, but a few decent eaters. Biggest 21". Tough at times as it’s been a tad WINDY. Also … Scotty making love to a sheepshead.

Nice day today so changed my timing belt. First time I’ve done this job so thought I share my experience.

There’s nothing to it. I already had some of the necessary tools and acquired what I didn’t.

Used an electric mid range impact to remove the flywheel nut.

I aready had a cheap flywheel puller which is necessary. Pressure on the puller and a few taps with a nylon hammer and the flywheel pops right off.

Everything under the flywheel comes right off without issue. I had an inch pound torque wrench, so I torqued all the fasteners. You could probably do this by feel if your gentle.

Next was replacing the flywheel. The nut has to be torqued to 115 ft-lbs (stamped right on the flywheel). I already had an 200 ft-pd torque wrench but no way to hold the flywheel. Yamaha sells a flywheel holder which is a fairly expensive tool with no other real use.

I saw some YouTube videos where they stuffed a rag between the flywheel and starter or a rope down the sparkplug hole. I wasn’t too keen on either.

I bought a Lisle 23800 Flywheel turner hoping it would hold the flywheel to torque it. I found some comments online that suggested it would work but I didn’t find where anyone said it would definitely work.

Looking at the tool, I had my doubts that it would grip the flywheel well enough for the torque needed. It absolutely works. It’ll certainly work on anything 50hp and under. I’m sure you can go higher depending on the diameter of the flywheel. It gripped securely with no hint of slippage.
The spring holds it in open or closed position.

Now that I know what I’m doing, the entire job would take about twenty minutes.

Real easy job, if you have or can borrow the tools.

Yesterday, Dec 16th, I was on Quinte ice for the first time this season at Deseronto. I don’t go out on early ice unless somebody is already out there. There were three pop ups out there about 300 meters off shore south of the Deseronto Yacht club (end of Mill street), so I went out. There was about 5 and a half inches of ice so it seemed safe enough where I was. Caught one small perch. If you go further southwest toward Foresters island the water is deeper, there is more current and the ice can get thinner quite abruptly. The weather for the next few days is going to make things more dicey.. Hopefully things will improve if it gets cold enough next week. Be very careful, Check with a spud every few meters. Foot traffic only.
Thanks for the ice report pdubya, i appreciate these. I been waiting for a few of these to come in.

I find it useful to use the NOAA satellite images to check for ice cover early in the season.

Noaa costwatch great lakes

You get the image with the following sequence

choose the MODIS product

Select Dataset Lake Ontario

year 2025

month december

click on a thumbnail where the image is clear. Most images are cloudy but the image for Dec 8 2025 is usable and shows ice cover on the Bay of Quinte from Trenton to Deseeronto wtih open water at the mouth of Hay Bay.

Of course you can’t tell how thick the ice is but ice cover is a good start, and you don’t have to drive anywhere to check things out.

Coastwatch Great Lakes Node

MODIS

MODIS (or Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) is a key instrument aboard the Terra (originally known as EOS AM-1) and Aqua (originally known as EOS PM-1) satellites. Terra’s orbit around…
